annual.due: By April 15 each year, starting the year after the LLC is formed.

amount.note: The Secretary of State lists the annual report fee for domestic and foreign LLCs. The first report is due by April 15 of the year after the articles take effect.

notIncluded.label: Reinstatement after dissolution
notIncluded.reason: Only if the LLC is administratively dissolved, for example for not filing annual reports.

sources.title: North Carolina Secretary of State - Fees: Limited Liability Companies

notIncluded.label: Registered agent service
notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Name reservation
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Reserving a name before you file is a separate charge and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Expedited filing and certified copies
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing and certified copies cost extra and are not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

notIncluded.label: Federal and state income taxes
notIncluded.reason: Taxes on the LLC's or its owners' income are not part of this estimate. This page is not legal or tax advice.

content.intro: {state} charges a one-time fee to file Articles of Organization and an annual report fee each year after the year the LLC is formed.

howItWorks.text: The Secretary of State's fee list gives the fee for Articles of Organization and for the annual report.
The annual report is due by the middle of April each year after the year of creation.

faq.q: Does a new {state} LLC file an annual report in its first year?
faq.text: No. The first report is due in April of the year after the articles take effect.
